title: Lesson 1: What an Agent-Implementation Consultant Actually Does
description: The agent-implementation consultant arc in one lesson: what an engagement looks like, what you actually deliver, and why this is not the same job as building agents for yourself.

questions.question: What mainly separates an agent-implementation consultant from a builder?
options: The consultant keeps sole ownership and maintains the agent forever
The consultant designs to personal taste instead of a contract
The consultant implements for a client and hands it over
The consultant builds only for their own product and its users
questions.explanation: A builder makes agents for themselves or a product; a consultant implements for a client and must leave that client able to run the system without them.

questions.question: What does the discovery and scoping phase produce?
options: A written scope and an honest go or no-go call
A trained client team and the handed-over keys
A validation record of real cases and safe failures
A running agent in production with monitoring in place
questions.explanation: Discovery and scoping end in a written scope and an honest decision about whether an agent is the right answer, before any building starts.

questions.question: Why is building before scoping a trap in a consulting engagement?
options: It is faster and lowers the client's total cost
The client is not obliged to pay for work that was never agreed
Scope grows on its own once the agent is running
A working demo removes the need for a written definition of done
questions.explanation: Without an agreed scope the client never committed to what you built, so it is under no obligation to pay for your guess.
